notes.title: Quick patch to fix helm controls
notes.content: Helm wasn't working correctly; the joystick code was overriding the keyboard and mouse controls.  I believe this is fixed now.

notes.title: Version 1.0.6 update
notes.content:
Thank you for purchasing Artemis Cosmos!  We've been continuing to improve it; this new version should have welcome improvements.

The font change resulted in multiple formatting problems, which have been fixed
The 3d view for fighters and weapons had some crashing and drawing issues
The controls for zooming the 2d radar have been changed
You can now CTRL-P paste into the client ip type-in box
new radar display for ship helm and fighter control
For helm, there are new hot keys: "impulse-up"  , PAXKEY_B, "increase impulse by 20%"))
                                  "impulse-down", PAXKEY_V, "lower impulse by 20%"))
Tuned the framerate to make the game work better, and stress the videocard less
significant script refactoring behind the scenes
several crash issues have been fixed
many other bug fixes, data cleanups, and minor corrections

notes.title: Update for 1.0.1. Merry Christmas!
notes.content:
brand new font rendering code; it should look better
Sometimes players would click the main screen controls (lrs, tactical, data) but nothing would happen; that's fixed.
Players complained that, when clicking something on the 2d radar view, the "lock" that moves the 
	view to follow the players' ship would disengage; it was too sensitive.  I added a slider in the
	UI Options screen to adjust the sensitivity.

notes.title: Cosmos Update, version 0.9.26
notes.content:
In the past three months, we've been working hard and making many significant changes. Sometimes the bugs and crashes never stop, but we're releasing a stable version (we hope) with many improvements.

On Science, we put the scan button back; the auto-scan system we had before was simply inelegant.  The science testers were unable to use it smoothly.

On Comms, we really wrestled with the GUI layout.  There's a 2d radar on Comms now, specifically for ordering friendly ships around.

The jump drive is in, and seems to work well.  It's currently only available on Ximni player ships.

Manual beam control is in, so the weapons officer can hit the buttons and target enemy ship systems.

We got fullscreen mode, and DMX lights, working very well.

And we added a new and fun little mission, Secret Meeting, to challenge you.

Along the way, we've been conquering bugs in every aspect of the code, making the network layer, the 3d graphics, and the GUI all better and prettier.

new mission, Secret Meeting
new comms control of friendly ships
manual beam controls
fullscreen option
DMX lights verified working
Ximni jump drive
Put scan button back on science

many, many bug fixes

notes.title: New update to Cosmos!
notes.content:
In the past six months, we've been beavering hard and making many significant changes.  I actually thought we'd aim for a 1.0 release that had a great deal less content and functionality than we do now.

I really didn't plan to put any space monsters or fighters into the game before 1.0.  However, the game's new, more universal and flexible approach to player ships meant that after building out the full 3d controls, it wasn't much more work to make player fighters, so they went in.

Similarly, the space monster was just a simple (but very configurable) use of some specialized drawing code, and a bit of scripting.

Along the way, we've been conquering bugs in every aspect of the code, making the network layer, the 3d graphics, and the GUI all better and prettier.

cinematic mode
you can nw click on the radar to steer your ship!!  Some people want that!
major overhaul to comms message waterfall
Torgoths have drones
Arvonians have fighter wings
Skaraans have cloaking and other special abilities

many, many bug fixes

notes.title: Update! Artemis Cosmos Version 0.9.0 (Early Access Release)
notes.content:
We've been hard at work through the end of summer and all of fall, and we're very happy to bring you this latest public release.  Because it's the second release of the game into Early Access, virtually every part of the game has been improved.



Helm's joystick integration is much more seamless, now.  Keyboard, mouse, and joystick control all work together without interference.   the 2d radar display that multiple consoles rely on has been changed to show all the new anomalies/pickups properly, and to handle mouse zoom and drag properly.

One of the things (on helm) that hasn't changed much is the "easy mode" control scheme, which allows limited y-axis movement.  This doesn't mean that 3d movement is impossible or secondary.  The 3d movement GUI modes we've been building simply aren't ready for release.  However, the future intent is certainly to give experienced helms officers complete 3d freedom of movement, as well as normal 3d fighter movement.

Weapons console gets a new fire mode that lets the weapons officer trade beam power for beam speed.  This can really help when Torgoth drones are coming in fast and heavy.  Weapons can see more combat effects (like beam fire and explosions) on their radar.  We've spent some time prototyping an upgrade of replacement for the old manual beam targeting GUI, but we haven't reached consensus, and we don't want to build any pointless minigames that waste your time.

We've listened to everyone who noticed how anemic the nukes were, and we've adjusted that.  There's still a problem with the EPM torpedos, but we'll get that fixed soon.

The most radical changes you'll see are on the Engineering console, where we're advanced the internal ship display, and the complex underlying simulation.  Now the ship hull is filled with complex spaces, and damage control parties that are much smarter than in the old game.  The damcon units have a lot more to say now, too.

We also listened to everyone, and re-added the coolant "dots" to the GUI.

Science information and scans are much more solid and informative.  Enemy shield weakness information is now available, and it works.  Science has a MUCH larger visibility range, which means more data for the science officer to parse, but we continue to make the GUI better and more supportive.  Engineering can boost sensors, which lets science see even farther.

Comms has working taunts and surrenders, friendly ships can be guided with a new graphical display, and stations can be told what torps to make.  Several improvements have been made to the comms GUI, but the most work has been done under the hood, improving the enemy AIs and the conversations the comms officer can have.

Red alert works.

So many bugs have been found and squashed.  The main to-do list is still pretty full.  But the game is more playable than ever,   If every bug were fixed, we'd be releasing 1.0.  But so much progress has been made, we feel the game is more playable than ever, and we didn't want to keep you waiting.  Enjoy!
